clue.text: See 14
Seen nightly, a performance apart from this?

indicators.note: a performance is a show put on, so these letters are staged in a new order

explanation.surface: A show that runs every night, and the question of what else could be on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a performance' is the anagram signal working on the twelve letters of SEEN NIGHTLY A; the definition is a shopkeeper's question.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop assistant asking whether you want more besides this item uses exactly this phrase.

clue.text: See 17
Barbarian passing round rugby posts in game

indicators.note: something passing round another surrounds it, so the barbarian word goes around the posts

parts.note: a peasant is a boor, an uncultured barbarian
rugby goalposts are shaped like the letter H

explanation.surface: A Barbarians rugby player runs round the posts during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: The Barbarians are a famous invitational rugby team, so 'Barbarian' reads as a player here, not a boor.
explanation.definitionFit: Game is the collective term for wild birds and animals shot for sport, and this bird is a classic example.

clue.text: A burden in the other half of clues?

definitions.text: in the other half of clues?

parts.note: a cross to bear is a burden

explanation.surface: Someone complains that one half of a crossword's clues is a burden.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a Down clue, so the other half of the clues is the horizontal set.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword clues come in two sets, and the other set from Down is the horizontal one, named by this word.

clue.text: End of the month coming up, give up

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters are read from bottom to top
the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: Dec is the short form of December

explanation.surface: At the end of the month, someone finally gives up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of' takes only the E of 'the'; that and DEC make EDEC, which 'coming up' turns around.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield or surrender something, such as territory, is a synonym of giving it up.

clue.text: One enforcing law from on high set free by doctor

definitions.text: One enforcing law from on high

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
to untie is to set free

explanation.surface: A lawman on high is released from bonds by a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places the doctor beside the freeing.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police polices from horseback, high above the ground.

clue.text: Yellow knife seen regularly against dish

parts.note: yellow and chicken both mean cowardly

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the word knife, starting with the first

parts.note: v is short for versus, against

explanation.surface: A yellow knife is seen against a dish on the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen regularly' takes K, I and E from 'knife'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a well-known dish of breaded chicken breast stuffed with garlic butter.

clue.text: Turn back to discuss tackle

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

parts.note: kit and tackle both mean equipment

explanation.surface: Someone turns back to talk over a tackle in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' looks like a reversal signal; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A turn is a short act in a variety show, and a short comic sketch is the same thing.

clue.text: Further behind horse, a bridle

indicators.note: behind places the word for further after the others

parts.note: a hack is a horse for ordinary riding
more and further both mean additional

explanation.surface: Further back behind the horse hangs a bridle.
explanation.definitionFit: A hackamore is a type of bitless bridle used in Western riding.

clue.text: Layers from jazz great, first and last two missed

indicators.note: missing out the first two and last two letters of the jazzman's name

parts.note: Oscar Peterson was a great Canadian jazz pianist

explanation.surface: Layers taken from a jazz great, with some bits left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first and last two missed' drops OS and ON from OSCAR PETERSON.
explanation.definitionFit: Workmen who fit floor coverings in homes are layers of carpet.

clue.text: Head of monastery housed by token primate

indicators.note: something housed by another sits inside it, so the head letter goes inside the token

parts.note: a chip is a token used in gambling

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The head of a monastery is put up by a primate, a senior bishop, as a token.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primate' also means an archbishop, fitting the monastery surface.
explanation.definitionFit: This ape is a member of the primate order, alongside monkeys and humans.

clue.text: Showing willingness within small firm?

indicators.note: what lies within the small firm is its two letters with a joining word between them

parts.note: Co. is the short form of company, a firm
spelling out the firm's abbreviation as '...' supplies the joining word

explanation.surface: An employee shows willingness inside a small company.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke: what is within CO? Its letters, C 'and' O, so the joining word sits between them; the question mark flags this loose reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A positive, keen attitude to getting things done is described with this hyphenated phrase.

clue.text: Again, check on Jack's mate?

parts.note: re means on or concerning
a jack is a male donkey or ass, so its mate is jokingly a female ass, an ass-ess

explanation.surface: Someone checks once more on how Jack's friend is doing.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack here is a jackass, a male donkey; adding the feminine ending -ESS to ASS makes his mate.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaluate once more is to check again, the prefix re- meaning again.

clue.text: Broadcasting polemicist, white knave hit screens

indicators.note: to screen is to shield, so the hit word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to sock is to hit
hock is a white German wine
J is the jack or knave in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A white knave in a card game strikes from behind a screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'white' is a wine here, not a colour; the hit word opens after its first letter to take the wine and the card.
explanation.definitionFit: A radio presenter who provokes listeners with outrageous opinions is a controversialist on the airwaves.

clue.text: Warm pieces reversed

indicators.note: the word for pieces is read backwards

parts.note: pieces is slang for guns

explanation.surface: Warm pieces of something are turned the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosy and comfortably warm, as a person tucked up in bed, is a synonym.

clue.text: Appliance — of ice pack in bra?

definitions.text: Appliance — of ice pack in bra?

parts.words: Appliance — of ice pack in bra?
parts.note: an ice pack kept in a bra would cool the bust

explanation.surface: A daft gadget: an ice pack tucked into a bra.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen appliance is a box-shaped freezer that opens from the top; the bra reading takes the first word as the bust.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large lidded kitchen appliance for frozen food, and the joke reads its parts as a body part kept icy.

clue.text: One of a pair held aloft, as a fisherman might?

definitions.text: One of a pair held aloft
definitions.meaning: a flamenco dancer holds clappers up in each hand, one of a pair
a fisherman might throw his net into the water, read as three words

explanation.surface: A fisherman raises one of a pair of nets above his head.
explanation.definitionFit: The percussion instrument is a pair of shells clicked together in each raised hand by Spanish dancers.

clue.text: See 20 down
Cheese pieces under flipped eggs

indicators.note: in a down answer, under places the pieces below the eggs
flipped means turned over, so the eggs word is read backwards

parts.note: nits are the eggs of lice
king and ... are both chess pieces

explanation.surface: A breakfast of cheese slices under fried eggs flipped over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipped' turns NITS into STIN; 'pieces' gives two chess pieces at once.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a pungent washed-rind cheese from Gloucestershire in England, famous for its smell.

clue.text: Testament very recently penned by setter, appropriate thing to say

indicators.note: something penned by another is enclosed by it, so the setter goes around the other pieces

parts.note: the setter of a crossword refers to himself as me
OT is the Old Testament
just means very recently, as in just arrived

explanation.surface: A setter has recently written a testament and found the right phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is French, 'the right word'.
explanation.definitionFit: This French phrase means precisely the right word or expression for the occasion.

clue.text: Finds book

definitions.meaning: decides as a verdict, as a court finds someone guilty
a book of the Old Testament following Joshua

explanation.definitionFit: A court that finds rules on a case, and the Old Testament book following Joshua bears this name.

clue.text: Pain in the neck, a don wants to batter molecular biologists

parts.note: a crick is a painful stiffness in the neck

indicators.note: battering something knocks it out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An irritating academic wants to hit the scientists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pain in the neck' looks like an idiom for a nuisance; here it is a literal neck ache. 'batter' rearranges A DON WANTS.
explanation.definitionFit: The pair of scientists discovered the double-helix structure of DNA in 1953 at Cambridge.

clue.text: Blasted thing, clergyman reportedly on crack

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard spoken, so the clergyman word is given by its sound

parts.note: a canon is a clergyman attached to a cathedral
a crack and a shot both mean an attempt

explanation.surface: A clergyman reportedly on crack cocaine, blasted out of his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blasted' looks like a mild curse; it means fired from a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A projectile fired, or blasted, from a large gun is the thing in question.

clue.text: See 20
A heart of white rose hollowed out — Yorkshire flower

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter
hollowing out a word leaves only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A white rose, symbol of Yorkshire, has its heart hollowed out.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'flower' is something that flows, a river: this one runs through Leeds. The white rose is Yorkshire's emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: A flower in crosswords is a river, and this one flows through Yorkshire.

clue.text: See 8
See 2
See 16
Club welcoming in king after retreat — like King Mark

indicators.note: a club welcoming something takes it inside

parts.note: a cosh is a heavy club used as a weapon

indicators.note: after a retreat the pair of in and king go backwards, so they are read in reverse

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A club admits a king after he retreats, like the legendary King Mark.
explanation.walkthrough: King Mark is the king of Cornwall in the Tristan and Isolde legend; Cornwall is England's south-western county.
explanation.definitionFit: King Mark ruled Cornwall in Arthurian legend, so he belongs to that county.
